title: Tasks
description: One checked Go core for personal GTD lists over JSONL, with CLI, TUI, and loopback HTTP adapters.
provenance: Authored 2026-09-11 from the Tasks codebase: the three composition roots (cmd/tasks, cmd/tasks-tui, cmd/tasks-api), pkg/tui, internal/*, docs/technical-architecture.md, docs/conventions.md, ADRs 0005/0006/0007/0010/0013/0015, and docs/plans/active. Relationships were traced through imports and call sites and then re-checked against `go list -deps` from every composition root; the same day an adversarial review corrected the first pass (dead term/frame packages, the merge-driver dispatch tier, the TUI adapter's non-blocking Pump, the harness reading task files). Known nuance recorded in the model: the CLI calls the store directly for every verb except capture and project complete/drop/reopen, which use the application facade; project create/rename/archive are also direct; the HTTP adapter uses two named store seams (checked read, changeset PATCH) documented in internal/api/seams.go and validates recurrence, lead, zone, and link inputs itself. Judgment calls: cli.prompt and tui.queue stay inside the agent-trust boundary as host-side orchestration that assembles prompts and spawns the harness, even though neither touches task data; store.journal is code, so it belongs to the persistence authority only and the durable-state boundary lists the on-disk XDG state directory instead. Parallel edges that make one claim share a title so the overview draws one line per claim; drilldowns keep every underlying relationship. Proposed content comes only from docs/plans/active. Not an exhaustive file inventory.

boundaries.title: Persistence and invariant authority
boundaries.description: The only code allowed to write task files. Owns the lock, canonical bytes, schema-v2 invariants, atomic replacement, rollback, revisions, and history.

boundaries.title: On-disk durable state
boundaries.description: User-owned task data and non-precious XDG state. Task files are the source of truth; the journal and sessions are recoverable.

boundaries.title: Agent and provider trust boundary
boundaries.description: Everything that assembles prompts for, spawns, or receives output from an autonomous harness. Agents read and act on task data only through the installed CLI; no private path crosses this line.

boundaries.title: Loopback network boundary
boundaries.description: 127.0.0.1 only: no remote bind, no auth mode, Host and Origin allowlists, forwarded headers refused, conditional writes required on task resources.

boundaries.title: Git merge driver process
boundaries.description: Git invokes tasks merge-driver with stage files through the early dispatch tier; the merge is built and checked entirely in memory with no configured store before it replaces Git's ours copy.

scenes.title: One Core, Three Surfaces
scenes.description: Tasks is a single checked Go core over JSONL files. The CLI, TUI, and loopback API are thin adapters; agents, Git, and Sidecar sit outside.

scenes.title: Inside the tasks CLI
scenes.description: Registry and dispatch tiers, the read, mutation, prompt, and maintenance verbs, and the merge-driver plumbing Git invokes. Which verbs use the facade and which call the store directly is stated on each card; the cli-mutation journey walks one write.

scenes.title: The Shared Application Core
scenes.description: What every surface agrees on: the command facade and its owned store seam, the read models, query semantics, temporal rules, and link classification. Surfaces and the store sit outside this focus.

scenes.title: Persistence and Invariants
scenes.description: Inside the store: exclusive lock, canonical records, invariant checks, atomic replacement with rollback, revisions, the undo journal, and the Git merge driver that reuses them. tasks.jsonl itself sits outside this focus; the cli-mutation journey shows a write landing.

scenes.title: The Loopback HTTP Boundary
scenes.description: Inside tasks-api: the loopback listener, transport gates, explicit routes, the If-Match precondition, and the two named store seams. The client and store sit outside this focus; the HTTP journey walks the full path.

scenes.title: Inside tasks-tui and the pkg/tui Surface
scenes.description: The standalone tasks-tui runtime, the shortcut registry, the agent prompt queue, session state, and the public pkg/tui surface a host such as Sidecar embeds.

scenes.title: Agent Adapters
scenes.description: The provider seam: the harness contract, the built-in harnesses, the system context assembler, and prompt facts. The spawn-and-act path is the agent-prompt and tui-agent-queue journeys.

scenes.title: Who May Write Task Files
scenes.description: The persistence authority is the only code that writes tasks.jsonl and archive.jsonl; the durable on-disk state around it is either the source of truth or recoverable.

scenes.title: Where Agents, HTTP, and Git Are Contained
scenes.description: Autonomous harnesses act only through the installed CLI, HTTP stays on the loopback interface, and the merge driver runs inside Git with no configured store.

scenes.title: Proposed: Subtasks in Context-Filtered Views
scenes.description: Planned TUI work from docs/plans/active: a matching descendant whose parent lacks the context keeps its ancestor chain, reusing the shared tree builder outside this focus. Sidecar's mapped-project capture defaults are the other open proposal, also outside this focus.
